You can't leave a `forEach` early. `break` is a syntax error in the callback, and `return` only ends the current call. An `await` in the callback doesn't make the loop wait either. A `for...of` loop has `break`, `continue`, `return`, and `await`.

The rule can't tell what's an array. It reports every method call named `forEach`, including on a `Map`, a `Set`, or a `NodeList`. Those work with `for...of` too.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"unicorn/no-array-for-each" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
users.forEach((user) => {
  if (!user.active) return;
  notify(user);
});
```

{/* bad */}
```js
lines.forEach((line, index) => {
  console.log(index + 1, line);
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
for (const user of users) {
  if (!user.active) continue;
  notify(user);
}
```

Use `.entries()` when you need the index:

{/* good */}
```js
for (const [index, line] of lines.entries()) {
  console.log(index + 1, line);
}
```

`Children.forEach()` and `React.Children.forEach()` aren't reported:

{/* good */}
```js
React.Children.forEach(children, (child) => {
  register(child);
});
```
